note: Media Thumbnails PDF ships one @MediaThumbnail plugin, MediaThumbnailPDF (id media_thumbnail_pdf, mime application/pdf), extending the parent media_thumbnails module's MediaThumbnailBase. On media save, media_thumbnails' hook_media_presave -> MediaThumbnailManager::createThumbnail() matches the source file's mime type and runs the plugin, which uses Imagick (needs the imagick PHP extension + a Ghostscript delegate) to render PDF page [0], flatten onto white, scale to the configured width, convert to JPG, and write a managed file at <source-uri>.jpg as the media thumbnail. It has no config of its own (configure=null), no permissions, no Drush, no config schema, no plugin types. Its behavior is tuned by the parent-owned media_thumbnails.settings (width default 500). Medium cases inspect that live settings config; hard cases set the width and (end-to-end) create a document media entity from a staged PDF so the plugin generates a real .jpg thumbnail, verified live. The document media type uses field_media_document; the full generation path was confirmed on the running site.

evals.prompt: In the Drupal contrib module media_thumbnails_pdf, what is the id of the thumbnail plugin it provides and which mime type does it handle?
evals.expected_output: It provides the MediaThumbnailPDF plugin with @MediaThumbnail id media_thumbnail_pdf, registered for the mime type application/pdf. It plugs into the media_thumbnails framework.

evals.prompt: What does media_thumbnails_pdf require in order to generate PDF thumbnails, and what happens if that requirement is missing?
evals.expected_output: It needs the ImageMagick PHP extension (imagick) — and in practice a Ghostscript delegate so Imagick can rasterize PDF pages. hook_requirements reports a requirement error if imagick is not loaded, and createThumbnail() logs a warning and returns NULL (no thumbnail).

evals.prompt: How is the width of a PDF thumbnail generated by media_thumbnails_pdf configured, and what image format is the generated thumbnail?
evals.expected_output: media_thumbnails_pdf has no settings of its own; the thumbnail width comes from the parent module's media_thumbnails.settings (the 'width' key, default 500), and the rendered page is scaled down to that width if wider. The generated thumbnail is a JPG written at <source-uri>.jpg.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, what thumbnail width will media_thumbnails_pdf use when generating a PDF thumbnail? Inspect the live configuration and give the number.
evals.expected_output: The width is read from media_thumbnails.settings; on this site it is 321 (drush cget media_thumbnails.settings width).

evals.prompt: This site has a custom background color configured for Media Thumbnails. Inspect the live media_thumbnails configuration and report the configured background color hex value.
evals.expected_output: media_thumbnails.settings has bgcolor_active TRUE and bgcolor_value #123456.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure Media Thumbnails so that PDF thumbnails generated by media_thumbnails_pdf are scaled to a maximum width of 250 pixels. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set the width the PDF plugin uses: drush cset media_thumbnails.settings width 250 -y (or \Drupal::configFactory()->getEditable('media_thumbnails.settings')->set('width', 250)->save()). media_thumbnails.settings.width must become 250.

evals.prompt: A one-page PDF file is staged on this Drupal site at public://mtpdf_eval/source.pdf and already has a managed file (File) entity (mime application/pdf). Create a media entity of type 'document' named 'mtpdf_eval' whose source field (field_media_document) references that PDF file, and save it so that media_thumbnails_pdf generates a thumbnail for it. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Find the staged file (e.g. loadByProperties(['uri' => 'public://mtpdf_eval/source.pdf'])), then Media::create(['bundle' => 'document', 'name' => 'mtpdf_eval', 'field_media_document' => ['target_id' => $fid]])->save(). Saving triggers media_thumbnails' presave hook, which runs the media_thumbnail_pdf plugin and sets the media's thumbnail to a generated JPG at public://mtpdf_eval/source.pdf.jpg.
